problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=Z\times Z$ in the Cartesian plane?

examples.knowledge_point: Sketching Cartesian Products of Special Sets in the Coordinate Plane
examples.problem: Sketch a representation of the set $S = \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{N}$ in the Cartesian plane.
examples.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A \times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B = \big\{(a,b) \::\: a\in A,\, b\in B\big\}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S = \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{N}
$$

contains every point in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose $x$-coordinate is an integer number and whose $y$-coordinate is a natural number.

$$
S=
\Big\{ (x,y) \: : \: x\in \mathbb Z,\, y\in \mathbb N\Big\}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider $S_1\subset S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any integer number and whose $y$-coordinate equals ${\color{red}{1}}.$

$$
S_1 = \Big\{ (x, {\color{red}{1}}) \: : \: x\in \mathbb Z\Big\}.
$$

We can represent $S_1$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/6b63e973bbcc3e25d601a1f6cef97f5a00cc22e738c46d04a1ac06851421894e.png)

Next, consider $S_2\subset S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any integer number and whose $y$-coordinate equals ${\color{blue}{2}}.$

$$
S_2 = \Big\{ (x,{\color{blue}{2}}) \: : \: x\in \mathbb Z\Big\}.
$$

We can represent $S_2$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/f24ce8f7610d096c795a8a74b0b714b720c36442042c28b66432d6b2102fb9d4.png)

We can create the subsets $S_3,S_4,S_5,\ldots,$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}\cup {S}_{3}\cup {S}_{4}\cup … \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in N}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{N}$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/c999c61d8ffbb27d47272811e32340cef3253b4730e684be10615487a8b27200.png)

feedback.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S={-1,3}\times [-2,1]$ in the Cartesian plane?
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S={-1,3}\times [2,1]
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is either $-1$ or $3$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-2,1].$

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in {-1,3},\,y\in [-2,1]}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-2,1].$

$$
{S}_{1}={(-1,y)\,:\,y\in [-2,1]}
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/57cb74832a9766c60819bdcc0c88290c4a05556b673965973e161895de2f530a.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{2}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $3$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-2,1].$

$$
{S}_{2}={(3,y)\,:\,y\in [-2,1]}.
$$

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/9f3d0beca2ed9eb30eb6456b67d5f17002726e9b9de6e8ed3c79d72f43bcf3ae.png)

Our Cartesian product is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
S={S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}
$$

Therefore, $S$ can be represented by the two line segments shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/d19ecceb011b54492d3ea9f0d262de1ba96e21c3423ed8b083d44551a6420db9.png)
